subject: Quantica: Dedicated GPU strategy — three-tier proposal (H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Zhou <kai.zhou@quantica.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantica: Dedicated GPU strategy — three-tier proposal (H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs)

Hi Kai,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Based on Quantica's mix of latency-critical triage flows and large-batch re-ranking jobs, we've sketched a three-tier Dedicated plan that balances memory needs, per-token latency, and unit cost. I've attached a spreadsheet with scenarios; summary below.

Executive summary (3 tiers)
- Tier 1 (H100-heavy): latency-first for live triage paths that require long context and complex reasoning. Best memory and throughput for very large models; higher unit cost.
- Tier 2 (A100-mixed): workhorse for large but not extreme context lengths. Good throughput for medium-context tokens and a reasonable cost compromise.
- Tier 3 (L4 burst & inference): cost-efficient for short-context, high-volume embeddings and low-latency pathways; limited memory for >32k tokens.

Key tradeoffs to confirm:
1) Memory headroom: do you have any >64k token flows that must remain on a single request (not cached/sharded)? If yes, H100 required.
2) P99 latency SLOs for the triage path — is 120ms P99 for generation acceptable for Tier 1? We can push lower but it increases cost.
3) Nightly batch re-ranking: we propose pinning to A100 reserved pool to lower cost while keeping predictable throughput.

Operational fallbacks and hedging:
- Auto-failover policy: route to A100 when H100 pool is saturated (degraded latency but preserved correctness).
- Cache-first routing for L4 to absorb spikes and reduce token cost.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the three workload buckets and any immutable constraints (max context, required P99s)?
2) If we align, we'll convert the attached scenario into a firm reserved capacity quote and an ops playbook for fallbacks and cost controls.

Attaching: quantica_three_tier_capacity.xlsx (scenarios + cost models), quantica_SLA_note.pdf (proposed latency tiers and SLA language).

Best,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Kai Zhou <kai.zhou@quantica.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantica: Dedicated GPU strategy — three-tier proposal (H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear framing. A few clarifications from our side:
- We have a small subset of flows that occasionally need ~80k token context (medical record stitching). Those must be single-request correct.
- For triage P99, clinical team wants <=100ms if feasible; otherwise we need to document user-visible degradation.
- Nightly batch is flexible and can tolerate slower throughput if cost-efficient.

Questions:
1) Can you map the 80k token requirement to a single-host option? If not, what engineering tradeoffs do we accept (sharding vs streamable summaries)?
2) Pricing sensitivity: 20% cost delta matters for our finance approval. Can you give approximate per-token unit cost difference between H100 and A100 in your model?

We'd like to get an ops runbook draft before we lock a 12-month committed contract.

—Kai
Director, Platform Engineering | Quantica Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Zhou <kai.zhou@quantica.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantica: Dedicated GPU strategy — three-tier proposal (H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs)

Kai —

Quick technical answers:
1) 80k tokens: current single-device support depends on model and quantization. H100 (80GB) can host sharded pipelines or large sparse attention models, but for a single-request 80k we typically recommend model parallelism across two H100s or using sequence-slicing with a KV-store approach. That means we can present two options: (A) dedicated H100 pair per instance (higher cost, single-request correctness) or (B) controlled sharding with summary stitching (engineering changes).

2) Latency: getting to <=100ms P99 on H100 is possible for shorter generations (<=1k tokens). For long-form single-request inference at 80k, the end-to-end will exceed 100ms by an order of magnitude unless we change the user experience (streaming portions, progressive answers). We should set expectations: H100 gives best chance but not magic.

3) Cost deltas (rough ballpark for committed reserved pools)
- H100 pair (per effective slot-hour): ~2.2x unit cost vs A100-80GB single slot
- A100-80GB (per slot-hour): baseline
- L4 (per slot-hour): ~0.25–0.35x of A100 for short-context workloads
These numbers vary with utilization and batching — we'll surface a model in the spreadsheet.

Ops notes (what we'll include in the runbook)
- Placement policy: pin triage flows to H100 pool; overflow metrics trigger routing to A100 with documented degradation.
- Cache priming: pre-warm KV cache nightly for known patient cohorts to reduce cold-starts.
- Monitoring: token-level cost, per-route P50/P95/P99, and model-mismatch error rate.

I'll add a short engineering appendix to the spreadsheet to show the H100-pair vs sharded approach.

—Lauren
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kai Zhou <kai.zhou@quantica.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantica: Dedicated GPU strategy — three-tier proposal (H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs)

Kai, Jordan —

Adding cost and commercial framing from a deals perspective:
- If Quantica commits to a 12-month reserved capacity with a blended pool (H100:A100:L4 = 20:60:20), we can offer a 14% blended discount off list per-token priced in the spreadsheet.
- If you require H100 pairs for all 80k-token single-request flows, that pushes the H100 ratio higher; with that we can provide phased ramping credits to soften first-quarter spend.

Two alternative proposals to consider (commercially distinct):
A) Memory-first commitment: higher H100 percentage, guaranteed headroom, SLA credit tighter on latency. Suitable if clinical correctness on single-request 80k is non-negotiable.
B) Hybrid engineering-first: use sharding/summary to limit H100 needs, rely on A100 for most production traffic, and L4 for bursts. Lower committed spend and easier procurement.

We should surface both options in the commercial term sheet and the ops playbook. Jordan — can you please bind a short 30-minute ops + procurement review for Friday so we can walk Quantica through both paths and the cost model?

Thanks,
Priyom
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Kai —

Great notes and very helpful context. Proposed immediate plan:
1) Friday 11:00am PT: 30-min ops + procurement review (I'll send a calendar invite).
2) Quantica action: confirm whether the 80k flows are strictly single-request-correct or if you can accept a stitched/sharded path for an MVP (this materially affects H100 sizing).
3) Redwood action: finalise the two commercial paths (Memory-first vs Hybrid) and upload a redlineable term sheet + sample runbook to the shared Drive by Thursday EOD.

I've attached the two files again and included a link to a draft term sheet on DocuSign for review.

Looking forward —
Jordan
